reading: Two single 2-cells each shoot a full row and full column line of 2 to the grid border; the rectangle enclosed between the four lines is filled with 1.
verb: draw cross lines then fill box
why: every marker gets a horizontal and vertical line to the border in its own colour; the only enclosed background area (between the lines) becomes 1
invariants: cells outside the lines and box stay 0

reading: Each diagonal pair of equal 3-blocks gets two 8-blocks of the same size on the perpendicular diagonal through the pair's centre, 1.5 block sizes from the centre (clipped at the border).

slots.subject: each object = two same-size colour-3 blocks touching diagonally
slots.mark: block of colour 8, same size as one subject block
slots.place: on the other diagonal through the subject's centre, offset +-1.5*blocksize in both axes

why: input unchanged; added 8 cells are exactly the two rotated-diagonal blocks per subject

reading: Several full lines (rows, columns, diagonals) of different colours cross; the output is one row listing the line colours from bottom layer to top layer, read from which colour wins at each crossing.

slots.subject: the full one-colour lines of the input
slots.order: partial order from crossing cells: the visible colour is above
slots.output: 1xN row of colours, lowest layer first

why: at every crossing the later colour in the output row is the one shown

reading: Every odd-sized square of the main colour (1x1, 3x3, 5x5) gets its centre cell recoloured to the colour of the plus-shaped object; even squares are unchanged. The plus is erased in two pairs but kept in the third (condition unclear).

slots.subject: square objects with odd side length
slots.plus: erased to background in pairs 0,1, kept in pair 2

why: only centre cells of odd squares change, to the plus colour; even squares untouched

reading: Grey marks in the top row pick columns and grey marks in the right column pick rows; every crossing of a picked row and picked column (outside the top row and right column) becomes 2.

new_rows.name: cross
new_rows.datalog:
w(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
top(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0, w(W), X < W.
right(Y) :- w(W), cell(Y, W, C), Y > 0.
cross(Y, X) :- top(X), right(Y).

why: every cell (r,c) with a mark at (0,c) and at (r,W-1) is 2; nothing else changes

reading: Grey (5) shapes have background holes; each uniquely coloured piece whose shape exactly matches a hole moves into that hole, leaving background behind. Other pieces stay.

new_rows.name: fits
new_rows.datalog:
ocol(O, C) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C).
grey(O) :- ocol(O, C), C = 5.
ncol(C, count(O)) :- ocol(O, C).
uniq(O) :- ocol(O, C), ncol(C, N), N = 1.
piece(O) :- ocol(O, C), !grey(O), uniq(O).
oy0(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
oy1(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ox0(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ox1(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
hole(O, Y, X) :- grey(O), oy0(O, Y0), oy1(O, Y1), ox0(O, X0), ox1(O, X1), px(Y, X, C), C = 0, Y > Y0, Y < Y1, X > X0, X < X1.
hy0(O, min(Y)) :- hole(O, Y, X).
hx0(O, min(X)) :- hole(O, Y, X).
hn(O, count(Y, X)) :- hole(O, Y, X).
pn(P, count(Y, X)) :- piece(P), obj(P, Y, X).
cand(P, O, DY, DX) :- piece(P), grey(O), pn(P, N), hn(O, N), oy0(P, PY), ox0(P, PX), hy0(O, HY), hx0(O, HX), DY = HY - PY, DX = HX - PX.
miss(P, O) :- cand(P, O, DY, DX), obj(P, Y, X), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, !hole(O, Y2, X2).
fits(Y, X) :- cand(P, O, DY, DX), !miss(P, O), obj(P, Y, X).

why: each moved piece keeps its shape and lands exactly on the hole cells of a grey shape; its old cells become background

reading: Small coloured pieces with grey (5) connector cells are chained left to right: each grey joint is recoloured to the neighbouring piece's colour and pieces are shifted vertically so joints meet, shrinking the grid width.

slots.subject: the fragments separated by background columns
slots.joint: grey cells marking where consecutive fragments connect
slots.joint_colour: grey becomes the colour of the adjacent fragment
slots.output: fragments concatenated horizontally, vertically aligned at joints; width shrinks

why: output is the concatenation of input fragments with joints overlapped and grey replaced

reading: There are two 2x2 blocks of 2 among scattered 8s; output a 1x1 grid of 8 if a chain of 8s connects the two blocks, otherwise 0.
why: the non-background component containing one block contains the other exactly when the output is 8

reading: A triangle has one odd-coloured cell at the middle of its base; a line of that cell's colour is drawn from just past the triangle's apex, continuing in the base-to-apex direction to the grid border.

new_rows.name: inner
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
single(O) :- osize(O, N), N = 1.
shape(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 1.
touch(M) :- single(M), obj(M, Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, obj(S, Y2, X2), shape(S).
inner(Y, X) :- touch(M), obj(M, Y, X).

why: one straight line of the inner cell's colour, on background only, from the apex side of the triangle to the border; direction is base-centre to apex

reading: The whole foreground shape moves down by one row.
why: every fg cell (y,x) appears at (y+1,x) with same colour; shape kept
